title: Pietro vs David Howell
informationNeeded: A PGN or complete FEN with side to move and board orientation, or clear full-board frames covering the relevant endgame.
reviewNotes: Physical-board game recap with changing camera views, missing board areas, and hand occlusion. Captions summarize the game rather than specifying every move.
transcript: This guy's a chess grand master, and I am rated 1750. I play with white, and I go for a London system, which my opponent is not happy to see because this is considered a boring opening. But, it is going to take more than boredom to defeat a chess grand master. But, I have studied this opening extensively, and this allows me to feel pretty confident from the opening and gain some significant time advantage on the clock. But, it doesn't take too long before I start being unsure about my moves, and that is exactly when I make my first mistake. The pawn push looked because I forced the knight to retreat, but the knight is going to find another route in the game, and now my bishops are blocked. And once the queens come off the board, we are now in David's territory, an end game. And all of a sudden, out of nowhere, everything in the position collapses. He takes my knight and then wins a pawn in the center, and I find myself without any good move to play. The grand master closes the position completely, this allowing my bishop and rooks to enter the game. And once his rooks are doubled on the A file, checkmate becomes unstoppable, and so I resigned the game, demonstrating why I am not a grand master.
